title: D6_6c-06 | ERD retrofit decision: new PX, degraded PX, PaT or low-pressure expansion
question_prompt:
D6_6c-06 | ERD retrofit decision: new PX, degraded PX, PaT or low-pressure expansion

Parallel benchmark: simulate_ro ∥ simulate_swro_system → joint feasibility and ranking

Operating context
The membrane train can meet production, but the plant must choose an energy-recovery retrofit. The first three packages share identical membrane conditions and differ only in ERD; the fourth uses low-pressure expansion. The membrane branch confirms quality while the plant branch differentiates energy.

Candidate design packages (same row sent independently to both simulators)
ID | Package / season | Pressure (bar) | RO module area (m²) | Plant RO area (m²) | Temp. (°C) | A (m/s/Pa) | B (m/s) | ERD | Efficiency | Annual weight
A | New PX, 95% | 65 | 60 | 6000 | 25 | 4.2e-12 | 3.5e-08 | PX | 0.95
B | Degraded PX, 86% | 65 | 60 | 6000 | 25 | 4.2e-12 | 3.5e-08 | PX | 0.86
C | PaT, 85% | 65 | 60 | 6000 | 25 | 4.2e-12 | 3.5e-08 | PaT | 0.85
D | Low-pressure expansion PX | 60 | 70 | 7000 | 25 | 4.2e-12 | 3.5e-08 | PX | 0.95

Task and decision rule
Meet membrane water ≥0.390 kg/s, NaCl ≤320 mg/L and inlet CP ≤1.35, plus plant product flow ≥0.043 m³/s and SEC ≤3.10 kWh/m³; choose the feasible package with the lowest SEC.

Required deliverables
1 | Run simulate_ro once for every candidate/season row and report water flux, membrane water flow, permeate NaCl, recovery and inlet CP.
2 | Independently run simulate_swro_system once for every candidate/season row and report plant product flow, SEC, LCOW and CAPEX.
3 | Join the two result branches by candidate ID, apply all constraints, and recommend one package.
4 | Explain why at least two non-selected alternatives fail or rank lower. Do not infer plant energy from membrane flux.
reference_answer:
Gold answer | D6_6c-06

Validated simulator outputs and joint decision

Final engineering conclusion
Recommend A, a new 95% PX. A and B have identical compliant membrane results, but A uses 2.786 kWh/m³ versus 3.044 for the degraded PX; the PaT package is rejected at 5.503 kWh/m³. D has the lowest SEC at 2.605 but cannot be selected because its 338.6 mg/L permeate exceeds the 320 mg/L contract limit.

tool_efficiency_rubric.reference_trajectory:
Tool efficiency | D6_6c-06

Reference trajectory for parallel multi-simulator work

Preferred tool trajectory
Step | Branch | Action | Calls | Why it is efficient | Common failure
1 | Shared | Create candidate packages and lock the module-to-plant scale mapping. | 0 | Prevents package drift between branches. | Changing pressure, area or membrane between calls.
2 | A | Dispatch all simulate_ro calls independently; retain package IDs. | 4 | One call per row; no unnecessary serial dependency. | Using simulate_ro for SEC or LCOW.
3 | B | Dispatch all simulate_swro_system calls independently; retain the same IDs. | 4 | Plant energy and cost come from the proper whole-system model. | Estimating plant energy from flux.
4 | Join | Join by candidate ID and evaluate all hard constraints. | 0 | Only combines results after both branches finish. | Mixing results from different candidates.
5 | Decision | Filter infeasible options, rank the survivors, and explain rejections. | 0 | Produces an auditable engineering recommendation. | Ranking by SEC/LCOW before quality filtering.

Efficiency verdict
Reference budget: 4 simulate_ro calls + 4 simulate_swro_system calls. Extra calls are justified only for correcting an error or testing a clearly stated sensitivity. equilibrate_feed is not needed because no mineral-speciation or scaling constraint is present.
